newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-FORECAST-North profit slip seen ending.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FORECAST-North profit slip seen ending.

text.p: Australian mining and forestry group North Ltd is expected to call an end to a prolonged profit slide when it announces its half-year earnings on Friday.
Stock analysts told Reuters on Thursday they expected net profit before abnormals to increase to between about A$46 million and A$54 million for the six months to December 31.
North reported a pre-abnormal net profit of A$41.2 million for the same period a year ago, culminating in a drop in annual net profit for the full year ending last June 30.
The group, which draws about 40 percent of its income from iron ore production, has been dogged by weak commodity prices, a stong local dollar and fairly static production volumes.
Net earnings for the first quarter of 1996/97 also fell.
But three stock analysts contacted by Reuters said they expected improved performances at North's uranium and copper operations to help give the group a stronger second quarter.
North's uranium subsidiary, Energy Resources of Australia Ltd, reported on Thursday a higher than expected net profit of A$15.2 million for the first quarter of 1996/97.

North's first-half production figures will be released with the group profit results on Friday, but a Melbourne-based analyst said he expected them to show higher output at the Northparkes copper-gold mine in New South Wales.
"We have had a higher dollar and low prices in a couple of areas, although copper has been reasonable," the analyst said.
The three analysts forecast full-year net earnings before abnormals of around A$120 million for 1996/97, compared with A$111.6 million last year.
The market is tipping an average annual pre-abnormal net profit of A$125 million for 1996/97, according to a December 31 survey of analysts by Barceps forecasting service.
"Overall the full-year profit would be flat to slightly up," said another analyst who did not want to be named.
